_note:
THE FOURTH INCIDENT ON THIS FLOOR AND THE FIFTH PROCEDURE FAMILY. Cold storage level 2 now carries a thing that hunts heat, a thing that stops when you look at it, a set of objects that does nothing, and this — a thing that occupies the warmest object it can reach and will not be watched while it rests on one.

§15.2 wants the building constant and the incident variable, and the fourth time round the point is no longer that the map is reused. It is that a squad walks in holding three operations' worth of correct knowledge about this floor and every piece of it is aimed at the wrong thing:

  · They know the 4.2m aisles need two staggered tripods to fence. Nothing here is fenced by heat, and a tripod set down near the case walls the case off from the anomaly entirely — the caller's file records what that costs.
  · They know a single camera at the south end of Aisle B holds the whole lane for free. A camera pointing anywhere near the case holds the operation OPEN, silently, until the case goes flat.
  · They know the office breaker is on the bay wall and the storage breaker is inside the office. Restoring the mains here does one thing: it makes the floor bright enough to look at things by, and looking at things is the failure mode.
  · They know the imager finds what is cold. There is nothing cold on this floor that matters. There are four things that are warm and one of them is a man.

The only habit that survives is the one nobody thinks of as a habit: get the case out and get it powered before you do anything else.
_spawnNote: It is on the contractor, and it has been since the Wednesday. That is not colour — it is the state machine's first state made physical, and it means the operation begins with the squad's first proper look at the body. `settled` exits on `noticed`, which is two continuous seconds of view; standing on the evidence source IS standing on the anomaly, and `sees` counts anything inside 0.35m regardless of facing, so a squad that walks up to take the observation starts the incident by taking it. Everything the floor has to teach about the rule is on the trail he left getting there.

briefing.headline: One fatality, one burn, cold storage level 2
briefing.report: Level 2 was mothballed eleven weeks ago with one mobile heater left running to keep the sprinkler main off freezing. The heater failed at 06:14 Tuesday. A contractor went down at 10:40 to replace it and did not come back up. Three men went down on the Wednesday to find him; they found him, and one of the three came back up with a burn nobody will describe. The floor was sealed that afternoon.

known.text: The contractor is at the north end of the west run, four days down, and the men who reached him say he was warm.
There has been exactly one powered object on this level for eleven weeks, and it failed on Tuesday morning.
The site's fixed camera at the head of the west run has been turned to face the wall and its lens taped over, from the aisle side, at some point after the floor was sealed. Nobody has claimed it.
The chiller return still reads under room temperature along its whole length. The plant has been off for eleven weeks.

_placementNote:
⚠ THE INVARIANT, NOT A FEELING. `contextAction` is nearest-wins and `sourceInReach` probes `reach + 0.6` = 2.8m, so two sources inside 2.8m of each other means the earlier one answers for both and the later one loses its verb entirely once the earlier is logged; and a source inside 2.8m of where an operative stands to work a breaker or a door beats the fixture outright, because it is nearer. That second kind has cost this project a whole operation once already — see the note in cold-storage-draught.json, where a charging rack 2.7m from the office breaker took the breaker's verb away and the solo containment could not get into the office.

So every source in this file was placed against a computed clearance rather than by eye:
  · > 5.0m (`reach` + probe) from BOTH door centres — freight (-8.0, -5.0) and office (-8.0, -9.75) — and from BOTH circuit switches — office (-6.0, -7.0) and storage (-10.0, -10.0). Beyond 5.0m a source cannot even be a candidate from any point at which the fixture is in reach, so it cannot win there: no ordering, no luck.
  · > 5.0m from the cargo cache (6.4, -7.2), which is a context candidate at `reach + 1.0`.
  · > 3.2m from every other source in this file, which is comfortably clear of the 2.8m probe and of section AF's 2.5m reporting margin.
MEASURED minimum across all ten: 3.40m source-to-source (fault printer ↔ thaw rings), 5.13m to any breaker or door centre (fault printer ↔ office breaker), 5.49m to the cache (residual heat).

The office desk is deliberately EMPTY in this incident. Three incidents have put a document on it and two of them are pinned there by the suite; the office is 3.8m square and already holds the storage breaker and a door, and this incident had no reason to add a fourth interactable to the most crowded room on the floor. Nothing here is in the office, the freight lobby, or the stair-head corner except the witnesses, who belong at a stair head.

THE SHAPE OF THE LAYOUT IS THE STORY IN THE ORDER YOU WALK IT. Three sources stand in a line up the west run — his work light where he set it down, the man 3.6m past it, his helmet camera 3.6m past him — so the west run reads as the last forty metres of somebody's Tuesday. The bay carries the paperwork and the two rings around the dead heater, which is where it started. The band of thawed floor across the aisle mouths is between the two, which is the route, and the imager is the only way to see it.
